# GitHub Pull Request #62

## Title
feat: load skills (SKILL.md), list them in the system prompt, and expand /skill:<name>

## Description
Closes #54.

pi-action now loads [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) the way pi's coding agent does. Docs: [`docs/skills.md`](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/feat/skills/docs/skills.md).

### Discovery (`src/skills.ts`)
- Searched in this order, and the first skill with a name wins (the others get a warning):
  1. Packages: those in `extensions`, then those in the new optional **`skills`** input (same spec syntax). Each package gives its `pi.skills` list, or else its `skills/` directory. Packages in `skills` are installed but **their code never runs**. A package that has only skills no longer gets the "has no pi extensions" warning.
  2. Project: `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Without it, the log says `Not loading the skills in .pi/skills: trust_project is off`.
  3. User: `<agent_dir>/skills/`, when `agent_dir` is set.
- Skills are found recursively. A directory with a `SKILL.md` is a skill, and its subdirectories are its resources, not more skills. Hidden directories and `node_modules` are skipped.
- Frontmatter is checked against the Agent Skills rules. `name` is required, uses `a-z0-9` and single inner hyphens, is at most 64 characters, and must match the directory name. `description` is required and at most 1024 characters. A skill that breaks a rule is skipped, and the warning gives the reason. `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill out of the prompt list but still allows `/skill:name`.
- There's no YAML dependency. A small parser handles top-level scalars: plain, quoted, multi-line, and `|`/`>` blocks. Nested maps are ignored.
- Setup log line: `Skills: release (project), deploy (project, /skill:deploy only), changelog (xyz-skills)`.

### Prompt section
- New built-in pi-durable extension `pi-action` (`src/builtin-extension.ts`). It is installed after `coding-tools` and before the user's extensions, so they can `wrapSection("available_skills", …)`. Its name is reserved. #53 can add the AGENTS.md section to it.
- `available_skills` uses the wording from the issue, with absolute locations and XML escaping. The section is left out when no skill is listed.
- The text is memoized per run. When the model sees `typescript` and no `read` tool (pit-only, #52), it says `workspace.read` instead of "the read tool".

### `/skill:<name> args`
- Replaces the task with `<skill name=… location=…>References are relative to <dir>.\n\n<body>\n</skill>\n\n<args>`, as pi does. This works in first messages, follow-ups and `prompt`, but not in answers. It runs before prompt-template expansion.
- An unknown name sets a new `Trigger.rejected`. `ThreadConversation` doesn't submit the trigger. Instead it replies with an error listing the skills, gets the 😕 reaction, and records it as posted so later runs don't post it again.
- The log shows `▶ … /skill:release 2.4.0 (skill from project)`. The comment entry stores `skill` and `typed`.

### Tests
- `src/skills.test.ts`: frontmatter parsing, discovery order and recursion, name collisions, each validation rule, section text and escaping, tool-aware wording, memoization, expansion and rejection.
- `src/extensions.test.ts`: `pi.skills` versus `skills/`, the `skills` input (including npm install and not running code).
- `src/run.test.ts`, end to end: system prompt, first-message and follow-up expansion, the `trust_project` gate, an unknown-skill error reply that isn't posted again.

### Docs
New `docs/skills.md`. Also updated: README (input table, docs table), `docs/extensions.md`, `docs/security.md` ("Skills from the repository"), `docs/prompts.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and CONTRIBUTING (source map).

### Known limitation
A run whose only request is an unknown `/skill:` still opens the thread, because `Thread.open` commits. The next request on that issue is then sent as a follow-up without the issue's context. Other runs that fail early on a new thread behave the same way.

`npm run check` passes (439 tests).

fix the merge conflicts and commitlint

## Your Reply

pi-action posts your final response as a comment on this issue or pull request. **Do not post your reply yourself**, for example with `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or `gh api`. That would post the same answer twice. Use `gh` to comment only where the task asks for it, such as on another issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.

+# Skills
+
+A **skill** is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file: instructions for one kind of task, and the scripts and files that go with them. pi-action loads skills as pi's coding agent does, from the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format:
+
+- The system prompt lists the name, the description, and the location of each skill. When a task matches a description, pi reads the full `SKILL.md`.
+- `@pi /skill:<name> <arguments>` puts the skill in the request itself. See [Use a skill explicitly](#use-a-skill-explicitly).
+
+Skills work in comment mode, `pr_number` runs, and direct prompts.
+
+## Where pi-action finds skills
+
+pi-action looks in these places, in this sequence:
+
+1. **Packages.** Each package in `extensions`, then each package in `skills`, in the order of the input: the `pi.skills` list in its `package.json` (files and directories, as `pi.prompts`), or else its `skills/` directory.
+2. **The project.** `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` in the repository, **only with `trust_project: true`**. See [Security](security.md#skills-from-the-repository).
+3. **The user.** `<agent_dir>/skills/`, when `agent_dir` is set.
+
+pi-action searches each directory recursively for directories with a `SKILL.md`. It does not search inside a skill (its subdirectories are its files), in hidden directories, or in `node_modules`.
+
+When two skills have the same name, the first one wins, and pi-action writes a warning. The log of the setup lists the skills, for example `Skills: release (project), changelog (xyz-skills)`.
+
+### The `skills` input
+
+`skills` loads packages for their skills only. It has the syntax of [`extensions`](extensions.md#declare-extensions): npm package specs or workspace paths, one per line or comma-separated, with `#` comments. pi-action installs npm packages in the same way, without lifecycle scripts, but it does not run their code. A package in `extensions` gives its skills too, so you do not have to write it in both inputs.
+
+```yaml
+- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
+  with:
+    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+    trust_project: true             # for .pi/skills and .agents/skills
+    skills: |
+      github:acme/xyz-skills#v1     # "pi": { "skills": ["./skills"] }
+```
+
+## Write a skill
+
+```text
+xyz/
+└── .pi/skills/
+    └── release/
+        ├── SKILL.md
+        └── scripts/bump.sh
+```
+
+`SKILL.md` starts with YAML frontmatter:
+
+```markdown
+---
+name: release
+description: Cut a release of xyz. Use it when someone asks for a new version.
+---
+
+# Release
+
+1. Run `scripts/bump.sh <version>`.
+2. ...
+```
+
+| Field | Rule |
+|-------|------|
+| `name` | Required. At most 64 characters: `a-z`, `0-9`, and single hyphens inside. The same as the name of the directory |
+| `description` | Required. At most 1024 characters. Write what the skill does and when to use it: the model chooses skills by their descriptions |
+| `disable-model-invocation` | Optional. `true`: the system prompt does not list the skill. It is available only as `/skill:<name>` |
+
+pi-action skips a skill that breaks these rules, and writes a warning with the reason. Write paths in a skill relative to its directory: the model resolves them against it.
+
+## The system prompt
+
+pi-action adds the `available_skills` section to the system prompt. Locations are absolute paths. Package skills are in `RUNNER_TEMP` (`pi-action-extensions-*`), where the coding tools can read them.
+
+```text
+<available_skills>
+The following skills provide specialized instructions for specific tasks.
+Use the read tool to load a skill's SKILL.md in full when the task matches its description.
+Resolve relative paths in a skill against its directory.
+
+  <skill>
+    <name>release</name>
+    <description>Cut a release of xyz. Use it when someone asks for a new version.</description>
+    <location>/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/.pi/skills/release/SKILL.md</location>
+  </skill>
+</available_skills>
+```
+
+- When the model has pit's `typescript` tool and no `read` tool (for example with `model_tools_hidden: read, write, edit, bash`), the second line says `workspace.read` instead of `the read tool`.
+- When no skill is listed, the section is not there.
+- The section stays the same for the whole run, so the prompt cache stays valid.
+- The section comes from pi-action's built-in pi-durable extension, `pi-action`. A pi-durable extension can change it with `wrapSection("available_skills", ...)` (see [Override tools and sections](extensions.md#override-tools-and-sections)).
+
+## Use a skill explicitly
+
+When the [task](prompts.md#the-task) starts with `/skill:<name>`, pi-action replaces it with the skill and the rest of the task:
+
+```text
+@pi /skill:release 2.4.0
+```
+
+pi gets:
+
+```text
+<skill name="release" location="/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/.pi/skills/release/SKILL.md">
+References are relative to /home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/.pi/skills/release.
+
+# Release
+...
+</skill>
+
+2.4.0
+```
+
+- pi-action removes the frontmatter. It does not replace `$1` or other variables, as it does for [prompt templates](prompts.md#prompt-templates).
+- This works in the first message (also `{{task}}` in `prompt_template`), in follow-ups, and in `prompt`. It does not work in answers to questions.
+- For a name that no skill has, pi-action does not send the request to pi. It replies with an error that lists the skills.
+- The log shows the request as it was typed, for example `▶ Request from @alice: /skill:release 2.4.0 (skill from project)`. The thread keeps the typed text in the `typed` field of the comment entry, and the name in `skill`.

+const MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 1024;
+const NAME = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/u;
+const FRONTMATTER = /^---\r?\n(?<yaml>[\s\S]*?)\r?\n?---[ \t]*(?:\r?\n|$)/u;
+const KEY = /^(?<key>[A-Za-z0-9_-]+):(?:[ \t]+(?<value>.*?))?[ \t]*$/u;
+const BLOCK = /^[|>][+-]?$/u;
+const INDENTED = /^[ \t]/u;
+const INDENT = /^[ \t]*/u;
+const LINE_BREAK = /\r?\n/u;
+const COMMENT = /\s+#.*$/u;
+const SKILL_COMMAND = /^\/skill:(?<name>\S*)(?:\s+(?<rest>[\s\S]*))?$/u;
+const XML_SPECIAL = /[&<>"']/gu;
+const XML_ENTITIES: Record<string, string> = {
+	"&": "&",
+	"<": "<",
+	">": ">",
+	'"': """,
+	"'": "'",
+};
+
+/** A YAML scalar as written in one line: quotes removed, `'` and `"` escapes resolved, a trailing comment cut. */
+function scalar(raw: string): string {
+	if (raw.startsWith('"') && raw.endsWith('"') && raw.length > 1) {
+		try {
+			return String(JSON.parse(raw));
+		} catch {
+			return raw.slice(1, -1);
+		}
+	}
+	if (raw.startsWith("'") && raw.endsWith("'") && raw.length > 1) {
+		return raw.slice(1, -1).replaceAll("''", "'");
+	}
+	return raw.replace(COMMENT, "");
+}
+
+/** A block scalar's lines (`|` keeps line breaks, `>` folds them), without their common indentation. */
+function blockScalar(style: string, lines: readonly string[]): string {
+	const indents = lines
+		.filter((line) => line.trim() !== "")
+		.map((line) => INDENT.exec(line)?.[0].length ?? 0);
+	const indent = Math.min(...indents);
+	const text = lines.map((line) => line.slice(indent));
+	if (style.startsWith("|")) {
+		return text.join("\n").trim();
+	}
+	return text
+		.join("\n")
+		.split(/\n[ \t]*\n/u)
+		.map((paragraph) => paragraph.replaceAll("\n", " ").trim())
+		.join("\n")
+		.trim();
+}
+
+/**
+ * The top-level fields of a file's YAML frontmatter, as strings: `key: value`, quoted values, values that go on in
+ * indented lines, and block scalars (`|`, `>`). Nested maps (`metadata:`) are left out. Undefined without frontmatter.
+ */
+export function parseFrontmatter(
+	text: string,
+): Map<string, string> | undefined {
+	const yaml = FRONTMATTER.exec(text)?.groups?.["yaml"];
+	if (yaml === undefined) {
+		return undefined;
+	}
+	const fields = new Map<string, string>();
+	const lines = yaml.split(LINE_BREAK);
+	for (let index = 0; index < lines.length; index += 1) {
+		const match = KEY.exec(lines[index] ?? "");
+		if (match?.groups !== undefined) {
+			const key = match.groups["key"] ?? "";
+			const value = match.groups["value"] ?? "";
+			const rest: string[] = [];
+			while (index + 1 < lines.length) {
+				const next = lines[index + 1] ?? "";
+				if (!(INDENTED.test(next) || next.trim() === "")) {
+					break;
+				}
+				rest.push(next);
+				index += 1;
+			}
+			if (BLOCK.test(value)) {
+				fields.set(key, blockScalar(value, rest));
+			} else if (value !== "") {
+				const more = rest.map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean);
+				fields.set(key, scalar([value, ...more].join(" ")));
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return fields;
+}
+
+/** Whether a frontmatter flag is true (`true`, `yes`, `on`, in any case). */
+function isTrue(value: string | undefined): boolean {
+	return ["true", "yes", "on"].includes((value ?? "").trim().toLowerCase());
+}
+
+function isDirectory(path: string): boolean {
+	return existsSync(path) && statSync(path).isDirectory();
+}
+
+/**
+ * The SKILL.md files at `path`: the file itself, or, in a directory, its SKILL.md, else the ones in its
+ * subdirectories, recursively. A skill's own subdirectories are its resources, not skills. Hidden directories and
+ * node_modules are skipped.
+ */
+function skillFiles(path: string, seen = new Set<string>()): string[] {
+	if (!existsSync(path)) {
+		return [];
+	}
+	if (!isDirectory(path)) {
+		return basename(path) === SKILL_FILE ? [path] : [];
+	}
+	const real = realpathSync(path);
+	if (seen.has(real)) {
+		return [];
+	}
+	seen.add(real);
+	const own = join(path, SKILL_FILE);
+	if (existsSync(own) && !isDirectory(own)) {
+		return [own];
+	}
+	return readdirSync(path)
+		.filter((name) => !name.startsWith(".") && name !== "node_modules")
+		.toSorted()
+		.flatMap((name) => {
+			const full = join(path, name);
+			return isDirectory(full) ? skillFiles(full, seen) : [];
+		});
+}
+
+/** Why a skill's frontmatter breaks the Agent Skills rules; undefined when it doesn't. */
+function invalidReason(
+	fields: ReadonlyMap<string, string> | undefined,
+	dir: string,
+): string | undefined {
+	if (fields === undefined) {
+		return "it has no frontmatter";
+	}
+	const name = fields.get("name") ?? "";
+	const description = fields.get("description") ?? "";
+	if (name === "") {
+		return "it has no name";
+	}
+	if (name.length > MAX_NAME_LENGTH || !NAME.test(name)) {
+		return `its name "${name}" must be at most ${MAX_NAME_LENGTH} characters of a-z, 0-9, and single hyphens inside`;
+	}
+	if (name !== basename(dir)) {
+		return `its name "${name}" is not the name of its directory, ${basename(dir)}`;
+	}
+	if (description.trim() === "") {
+		return "it has no description";
+	}
+	if (description.length > MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH) {
+		return `its description is longer than ${MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH} characters`;
+	}
+	return undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Loads the skills of every source, in order. A skill whose frontmatter breaks the Agent Skills rules is skipped,
+ * and when names collide, the first one wins; the log says which ones it skips.
+ */
+export function loadSkills(
+	sources: readonly SkillSource[],
+	log: Log,
+): Map<string, Skill> {
+	const skills = new Map<string, Skill>();
+	for (const { source, paths } of sources) {
+		for (const filePath of paths.flatMap((path) => skillFiles(path))) {
+			const baseDir = dirname(filePath);
+			const fields = parseFrontmatter(readFileSync(filePath, "utf8"));
+			const reason = invalidReason(fields, baseDir);
+			const name = fields?.get("name") ?? "";
+			const taken = skills.get(name);
+			if (reason !== undefined) {
+				log.warning(`Skill ${filePath} from ${source} is skipped: ${reason}`);
+			} else if (taken === undefined) {
+				skills.set(name, {
+					name,
+					description: (fields?.get("description") ?? "").trim(),
+					filePath,
+					baseDir,
+					source,
+					disableModelInvocation: isTrue(
+						fields?.get("disable-model-invocation"),
+					),
+				});
+			} else {
+				log.warning(
+					`Skill ${name} from ${source} is ignored: ${taken.source} has one with that name`,
+				);
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return skills;
+}
+
+const escapeXml = (text: string): string =>
+	text.replaceAll(XML_SPECIAL, (char) => XML_ENTITIES[char] ?? char);
+
+/**
+ * The text of the `available_skills` section: the skills the model may use, with how to read them (`read` names
+ * the tool or function that reads a file). Undefined when there are none.
+ */
+export function formatSkillsSection(
+	skills: Skills,
+	read: string,
+): string | undefined {
+	const listed = [...skills.values()].filter(
+		(skill) => !skill.disableModelInvocation,
+	);
+	if (listed.length === 0) {
+		return undefined;
+	}
+	return [
+		"The following skills provide specialized instructions for specific tasks.",
+		`Use ${read} to load a skill's SKILL.md in full when the task matches its description.`,
+		"Resolve relative paths in a skill against its directory.",
+		"",
+		...listed.flatMap((skill) => [
+			"  <skill>",
+			`    <name>${escapeXml(skill.name)}</name>`,
+			`    <description>${escapeXml(skill.description)}</description>`,
+			`    <location>${escapeXml(skill.filePath)}</location>`,
+			"  </skill>",
+		]),
+	].join("\n");
+}
+
+/**
+ * The `available_skills` section. It names the read tool, or pit's `workspace.read` when the model is offered
+ * pit's `typescript` tool and no `read` tool. The text is the same for the whole run, so the prompt cache holds.
+ */
+export function skillsSection(skills: Skills): PromptSection {
+	const rendered = new Map<string, string | undefined>();
+	return section("available_skills", (input) => {
+		const offered = new Set(input.agent.tools.map((tool) => tool.name));
+		const read =
+			!offered.has("read") && offered.has("typescript")
+				? "workspace.read"
+				: "the read tool";
+		if (!rendered.has(read)) {
+			rendered.set(read, formatSkillsSection(skills, read));
+		}
+		return rendered.get(read);
+	});
+}
+
+/** A skill's instructions for a request: its SKILL.md without the frontmatter, with its directory, as in pi. */
+export function skillMessage(skill: Skill, args: string): string {
+	const body = readFileSync(skill.filePath, "utf8")
+		.replace(FRONTMATTER, "")
+		.trim();
+	const block = `<skill name="${skill.name}" location="${skill.filePath}">\nReferences are relative to ${skill.baseDir}.\n\n${body}\n</skill>`;
+	return args === "" ? block : `${block}\n\n${args}`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The trigger with its task expanded, when the task starts with `/skill:<name>`: the skill's instructions, then the
+ * arguments. An unknown name rejects the trigger (`rejected`: the error to reply with); other tasks, and answers to
+ * questions, stay as they are.
+ */
+export function expandSkill(trigger: Trigger, skills: Skills): Trigger {
+	const match = trigger.answer
+		? undefined
+		: SKILL_COMMAND.exec(trigger.task.trim());
+	if (match?.groups === undefined) {
+		return trigger;
+	}
+	const name = match.groups["name"] ?? "";
+	const skill = skills.get(name);
+	if (skill === undefined) {
+		const known = [...skills.keys()].map((other) => `\`${other}\``);
+		return {
+			...trigger,
+			rejected: `There is no skill named \`${name}\`. ${known.length > 0 ? `Skills: ${known.join(", ")}.` : "No skills are loaded."} See https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/main/docs/skills.md`,
+		};
+	}
+	return {
+		...trigger,
+		task: skillMessage(skill, (match.groups["rest"] ?? "").trim()),
+		skill: { name: skill.name, source: skill.source, typed: trigger.task },
+	};
+}
